title: Problems — Carson Arbuckle
text:
Exploration
  Problems I'm Exploring
  Real challenges I've encountered as a student and professional. I'm actively thinking about how technology and better design could solve them.



  01
  
    Networking and Job Tracking
    
      The Problem
      Managing professional relationships and job applications is fragmented and overwhelming. Contacts live in LinkedIn, notes in spreadsheets, follow-ups in email, and application statuses in separate portals. Important connections fall through the cracks.
    
    
      Why It Matters
      As a strategic management student preparing to enter the workforce, I've experienced firsthand how difficult it is to stay organized during recruiting season. Missing a follow-up email or forgetting where you met someone can cost you an opportunity.
    
    
      The Opportunity
      A unified system that tracks contacts, conversations, application statuses, and follow-up reminders could transform how students and professionals manage their career development.
    
  



  02
  
    Time Blocking a Calendar
    
      The Problem
      Time blocking is one of the most effective productivity techniques, but actually implementing it is tedious. Manually dragging blocks around a calendar, estimating task durations, and adjusting when priorities shift takes more time than it saves.
    
    
      Why It Matters
      I've seen how powerful time blocking can be for staying focused and getting things done. But the friction of setting it up means most people abandon it after a few days.
    
    
      The Opportunity
      An intelligent system that helps you quickly allocate time based on your tasks, deadlines, and energy levels could make time blocking accessible to everyone — not just productivity enthusiasts.
    
  



  03
  
    Responding to Emails Efficiently
    
      The Problem
      Email remains essential for professional communication, but crafting thoughtful responses takes significant time. Many emails require similar responses, yet we write them from scratch each time.
    
    
      Why It Matters
      During my internships, I noticed how much time gets lost to email. It's not just about speed — it's about mental energy spent context-switching between tasks and inbox management.
    
    
      The Opportunity
      Smarter email tools that draft contextual responses, suggest follow-ups, and help batch similar communications could give professionals hours back each week.
    
  



  04
  
    Keeping Track of Assignments and Due Dates
    
      The Problem
      Students juggle multiple courses, each with its own syllabus, learning management system, and assignment schedule. Important deadlines get buried, and the mental load of tracking everything is exhausting.
    
    
      Why It Matters
      As someone balancing coursework with internships and extracurriculars, I've felt the stress of almost missing deadlines simply because information was scattered across too many places.
    
    
      The Opportunity
      A centralized dashboard that aggregates assignments from all courses, sends smart reminders, and helps prioritize based on weight and difficulty could reduce student stress and improve academic performance.
    
  



  05
  
    Alarms That Actually Wake You Up
    
      The Problem
      Traditional alarms are easy to dismiss or sleep through. Snooze buttons enable bad habits, and most alarm apps don't adapt to individual sleep patterns or wake-up difficulties.
    
    
      Why It Matters
      Consistent wake-up times are foundational to productivity, health, and success. Yet millions of people struggle with this basic daily challenge, often starting their day already behind.
    
    
      The Opportunity
      An alarm system that uses adaptive techniques — like requiring physical movement, solving puzzles, or integrating with smart home devices — could help people build better morning routines and take control of their days.

title: Business Case Presentation
text:
Problem Statement

Market Problem

Issue Identification: What specific problem does your product solve?
Target Audience: Who experiences this problem most acutely?
Current Solutions: How are people solving this problem today?
Gap Analysis: What’s missing from existing solutions?



Quantifying the Problem

Market Size: How many people/organizations face this issue?
Economic Impact: What does this problem cost users currently?
Urgency: Why is now the right time to solve this problem?
Evidence: What data supports the existence and scale of this problem?

title: Business Case Presentation
text:
Market Analysis

Industry Overview

Market Size: Total Addressable Market (TAM), Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM)
Growth Trends: Historical growth rates and future projections
Key Drivers: What factors are driving market growth?
Market Maturity: Where is this market in its lifecycle?



Competitive Landscape

Direct Competitors: Who offers similar solutions?
Indirect Competitors: What alternative approaches exist?
Competitive Advantages: How will you differentiate?
Market Positioning: Where will you fit in the competitive landscape?



Customer Analysis

Target Segments: Primary and secondary customer groups
User Personas: Detailed profiles of ideal customers
Buying Behavior: How do customers make purchase decisions?
Price Sensitivity: What are customers willing to pay?

title: Business Case Presentation
text:
Solution Overview

Product Vision

Core Value Proposition: What unique value do you provide?
Key Features: What are the essential product capabilities?
User Experience: How will customers interact with your product?
Differentiation: What makes your solution superior?



Product Strategy

Development Approach: Build vs. buy vs. partner decisions
Technology Stack: What technical foundation will you use?
Scalability: How will the product grow with demand?
Innovation: What makes this solution innovative?

title: Business Case Presentation
text:
Business Model

Revenue Model

Pricing Strategy: How will you price your product?
Revenue Streams: What are your sources of income?
Customer Acquisition: How will you attract customers?
Unit Economics: What are your cost and revenue per customer?



Financial Projections

Revenue Forecast: 3-5 year revenue projections
Cost Structure: Development, operational, and marketing costs
Profitability Timeline: When will you reach break-even?
Investment Requirements: Funding needed for different milestones



Go-to-Market Strategy

Launch Strategy: How will you introduce the product?
Marketing Channels: How will you reach customers?
Sales Strategy: Direct, partner, or hybrid approach?
Customer Success: How will you ensure customer satisfaction?

title: Business Case Presentation
text:
Implementation Plan

Development Roadmap

Phase 1: MVP development and initial testing
Phase 2: Full product launch and market entry

Phase 3: Scale and expansion opportunities
Milestones: Key deliverables and timeline



Resource Requirements

Team Structure: What roles and skills are needed?
Technology Infrastructure: What systems and tools are required?
Capital Requirements: Funding needs by phase
Strategic Partnerships: What alliances will accelerate success?



Risk Analysis

Market Risks: What could change in the market?
Technical Risks: What development challenges might arise?
Competitive Risks: How might competitors respond?
Mitigation Strategies: How will you address each risk?

title: Business Case Presentation
text:

Key Performance Indicators

Customer Metrics: Acquisition, retention, satisfaction
Business Metrics: Revenue, profitability, market share
Product Metrics: Usage, engagement, feature adoption
Operational Metrics: Efficiency, quality, scalability



Success Criteria

Long-term (3-5 years): [Vision achievement and expansion goals]

title: Business Case Presentation
text:
Investment Recommendation

Case for Investment

Market Opportunity: Large, growing market with clear need
Competitive Advantage: Defensible differentiation and positioning
Team Capability: Right skills and experience to execute
Financial Returns: Attractive risk-adjusted return potential
Strategic Fit: Aligns with organizational goals and capabilities



Expected Outcomes

Revenue Impact: [Projected revenue contribution]
Market Position: [Expected market share and positioning]
Strategic Value: [Broader organizational benefits]
Growth Platform: [Future expansion opportunities]

Long-term Goals (1 year)

Launch product to target market
Achieve customer acquisition targets
Demonstrate product-market fit
Plan expansion opportunities
